messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I used MSstats TMT some time ago and everything was working, but these days I was trying to analyze some data and I get the error:" ** Please check the annotation file. The channel name must be matched with that in input data."

I check some conversations in the group from people with the same problem, but the solutions they used did not work for me. I tried channelx and channel.x. but the error still happening.
Please,  what do I do?

Thank you so much

best
Debora

messages.subject: Re: How long should protein summarization step take?
messages.subject_clean: How long should protein summarization step take?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

it might be due to imputation step.
To possibly get the summary faster, please try setting MBimpute = FALSE first.
To identify the issue, as a first step I suggest finding proteins with a very large number of features and some missing values.
It is likely that the imputation step (AFT model via survreg function) takes most of the computation time for a few proteins with the largest number of features.

Kind regards,
Mateusz Staniak

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I think sometimes the same errors occurs if something goes wrong earlier in the process and all data is filtered before matching annotation to input. Can you try to find a very tiny subset of input data (like a single protein) that reproduces the issue?
Moreover, providing package versions (sessionInfo() output) and MSstats options that results in this error would help us locating the problem.

Kind regards,
Mateusz Staniak

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I took a look and your FASTA file seems to be missing all of the protein IDs contained in your evidence file.  To create a valid FASTA file, could you take all of the unique protein IDs in your evidence file, go to Uniprot ID mapping <https://www.uniprot.org/id-mapping>, and paste all of your IDs in the input box to create a FASTA file?

Thanks,
Tony

messages.subject: Re: RunLevelData is not available when I set remove50missing=TRUE in processData
messages.subject_clean: RunLevelData is not available when I set remove50missing=TRUE in processData
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Apologies for the delay.  A couple follow ups:
Are you able to upgrade to the latest version of R (R4.4) and MSstats (4.12.0)?  Your version looks to be outdated and I'm not sure if we can properly debug an old version of the package.
What's your understanding of how the "remove50Missing" parameter works?  According to our documentation <https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstats/blob/devel/man/dataProcess.Rd#L88-L89>, "remove50Missing = TRUE removes the proteins where every run has at least 50% missing values for each peptide", so very rarely should you see it doing anything to your dataset.
Thanks,
Tony

messages.subject: Missing Table from dataProcess function
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am currently running MSstats with timsTOF DIA-PASEF data from Fragpipe.  I have two conditions (no_cross and decross) and two bioreplicates for each condition.  After importing the data with FragpipetoMSstatsFormat, I am using the dataProcess to log transform, normalize the data, etc.  I have run the dataProcess function multiple times now and I keep getting back only two tables and the summary method ("FeatureLevelData" "ProteinLevelData" "SummaryMethod").

When I watch this YouTube video, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=30a6sDj8Qlo&list=PL2u38g_AG4MG_puKZBT4HawiVLQBE28gD&index=11, it looks like there should be more tables in the list (picture below with time stamp).

So, I am wondering if I am missing something.  Is my code wrong (pictured below)?  Is this a difference with MSstats 4.0 vs the older version?

Best,
Max

Hi,

I did some further debugging and the issue is related to having only 2 bioreplicates in your dataset.  By default, if the MaxQuant converter only observes 2 or less bioreplicates in a dataset, it will fail.

One question - what is the reason that this dataset has 2 bioreplicates only?

Thanks
Tony

messages.subject: peptide PTM annotation and sequence
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Something I have been wondering about: for some of the tools I would like to use following MSstatsPTM analysis, such as PTM-SEA or KinSwingR, I need the (centered) amino acid sequence surrounding the PTM site and the exact location of the PTM on the protein. However, this doesn't seem to be included in the output. Is there a way to achieve this with MSstatsPTM? Or perhaps an existing package that could be used to perform this mapping?

Kind regards,

Robin Colpaert
